Findings.Title: separate files defeat atomic stop-ledger enrollment
Findings.EvidenceAndFix: Plan locations: host row line 83; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004 line 213; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 line 223; TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 line 345; wire store lines 550-551; A7 line 587. **Defect:** cursor, queue and held sets are in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`, while stop entries are in separate `stop-ledger.yaml`; line 551 nevertheless promises the ledger entry is added in the same atomic replace that delivers or holds and advances the cursor. A single temp-file rename cannot atomically replace both. If cursor advancement persists and ledger writing fails, restart skips the cause record and the open request is invisible to the stop gate. A7's restart case does not inject a crash between these writes. **To PASS:** store ledger in the same atomic state file, or specify a journal/recovery protocol proving enrollment; propagate the one rule to host row, FR/TR, UC-1, wire, A3/A7, TODO and handoff. Add before/after each persistence-boundary and two-Stop restart RED cases with zero missed blocks. **Classification:** implementer plan/requirement/test edit under D5/D10; no new operator decision.
Findings.Classification: implementer plan/requirement/test edit under D5/D10; no new operator decision.

Findings.Title: held-set dissolution fabricates delivery
Findings.EvidenceAndFix: Plan locations: host row line 83; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 line 202; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009 line 248; A3 line 579. **Defect:** two equal-content queued requests R1/R2 followed by `popAll` with one matching line are held because the withdrawn identity is unknown. If R1 later closes explicitly, the plan dissolves the set and changes R2 to `delivered`. R2 could have been the request actually withdrawn. No `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` event proves its delivery. A3's named dissolve test enshrines the guess. The held-head `dequeue` rule also lacks exact FIFO membership and resolution semantics. **Evidence:** line 83 says the short `popAll` changes no candidate state, then promotes the last open candidate; enqueue and dequeue lack a shared identity with remove. **To PASS:** keep survivors unresolved until a traceable host event identifies them, or fail the host closed as `turn_logging_unsupported` under D6. Specify queue membership, cursor, close and recovery transitions; do not mark delivered solely because another candidate closed. Replace the dissolve test with two-equal/one-line-popAll/explicit-close/restart/dequeue tests proving zero wrong-turn writes. Propagate to FR/TR, wire, UC-1, TODO and handoff. **Classification:** implementer contract/test edit under D5/D6/D9; no new operator decision.
